statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-8924: when the URL uses a hostname with a trailing dot, a malicious HTTP server can set a cookie for a public suffix written with a trailing dot (for example domain=co.uk.), bypassing curl's Public Suffix List check, and curl then sends that super cookie to unrelated sites (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-8924.html). It affects curl 7.46.0 to 8.20.0 and was fixed in curl 8.21.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/51beed175dbfc37da3113f6acce60c630c070ce8, which trims trailing dots before the PSL check. As of 2026-11-27 the DHI curl packages for Alpine 3.23 are builds of curl 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. The DHI rebuild 8.20.0-r1 does not carry a backport of this fix: the machine code of the cookie module in the static libcurl.a shipped in curl-static (x86_64) is identical in 8.20.0-r0 and 8.20.0-r1, and changes in 8.21.0-r0. So 8.21.0-r0, the first build of curl 8.21.0, is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-8924: when the URL uses a hostname with a trailing dot, a malicious HTTP server can set a cookie for a public suffix written with a trailing dot (for example domain=co.uk.), bypassing curl's Public Suffix List check, and curl then sends that super cookie to unrelated sites (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-8924.html). It affects curl 7.46.0 to 8.20.0 and was fixed in curl 8.21.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/51beed175dbfc37da3113f6acce60c630c070ce8, which trims trailing dots before the PSL check. Debian backported the fix to trixie (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-8924, DSA-6558-1); the Debian changelog records it under 8.14.1-2+deb13u6. The DHI curl packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie curl 8.14.1-2; as of 2026-11-27 the DHI Debian repository publishes three of them (the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and two rebuilds of 8.14.1-2+deb13u7) for amd64 and arm64. The two rebuilds of 8.14.1-2+deb13u7 ship a changelog that records the CVE-2026-8924 fix; the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 does not have it. The first rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u7 is the fixed version used here.
